summary: Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He taught Eshin Nishimura and held posts at Otani University (~1928–1951) and Hanazono University (~1948–1974).
Zenno Ikuno (b. 1928) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Taisho University (~1949–1956). His posts included professor and professor emeritus at Taisho University, head of Jodo Shu Research Institute, and president of Shukutoku Junior College (2002–2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1938), Rissho University (~1938–1950), and University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) studied Buddhist studies and Sinology under Shinko Mochizuki, Keiki Yabuki, Benkyo Shiio, Jitsuzo Kuwabara, and Toru Haneda. He held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, and directed Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972).

Zensho Kitagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts at Rissho University as lecturer (attested 1976) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and was affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Zesho Machida is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post as betto at Kuon-ji (attested 1990) and served as professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Zev Handel works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Harvard College and the University of California, Berkeley, and became a professor at the University of Washington (~1999).
Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

Zhaohua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology who taught Kevin Buckelew. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and as a faculty member at Columbia University (attested 2018).
Zhen Liu works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed master's degrees at the University of Munich (by 2005) and Lanzhou University (by 2009).
Zhengyan Fan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Tianning Buddhist Institute (1947) and under Yinshun (1952), taught Chien Y. Hsu, and served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel and held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~2002–2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).

Zhiru Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi studied Buddhist studies and religious studies at the University of Arizona (PhD) under Robert M. Gimello. She held posts at Pomona College as associate professor (attested 2007–2014) and at Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

Zhiyi Yang is a Sinologist who studied at Peking University, the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Princeton University (PhD under Martin Kern). She held posts at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where she later served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied under Bai Su (~1953–1958). He served as director at The Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965). He held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University (~1998–1999).
